title: Hybridization of DNA Oligonucleotide Probes
author: Jonathan Houseley
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bns6mehe

steps.title: Clean oligonucleotide probe
steps.instruction: Use a QIAquick Nucleotide Removal Kit to clean the DNA oligonucleotide probe before labeling.

steps.title: Check hybridization bottles
steps.instruction: Inspect hybridization bottles and internal seals to ensure they are in good condition and will not leak radioactive buffer during hybridization.

steps.title: Prewarm ULTRAHyb solution
steps.instruction: Place a bottle of ULTRAHyb Oligo in a 68 °C water bath or oven and warm until the SDS fully dissolves (approximately 15–20 min, 00:15:00–00:20:00).

steps.title: Prepare membrane for hybridization
steps.instruction: Wet the membrane with 0.1× SSC containing 0.1 % SDS, roll it up with the RNA‑facing side inward, drop it into the hybridization bottle, slowly unroll it against the bottle wall, push out any air bubbles, and place the bottle in a rotating hybridization oven so the membrane edge moves with the rotation. Balance the bottles (including liquid volume) and, if desired, place two membranes in one bottle (one facing the glass, the other facing the bottle interior).

steps.title: Pre‑hybridize membrane
steps.instruction: Add 7.5 mL UltraHyb Oligo to the bottle and incubate the membrane for 1 h at 42 °C.

steps.title: Assemble labeling reaction
steps.instruction: In a micro‑tube combine in this order: 5 pM oligonucleotide (1.5 µL), 10× T4 polynucleotide kinase buffer (1.5 µL), 100 mM DTT (add water to bring total volume to 9 µL, i.e., add 1 µL water), T4 polynucleotide kinase (5 µL), and [γ‑32P] ATP (3000 Ci/mmol, 185 MBq/mL). The final volume should be 9 µL.

steps.title: Incubate labeling reaction
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture for 1 h at 37 °C (2 h or longer is acceptable).

steps.title: Purify labeled probe
steps.instruction: Pass the labeling reaction through a mini Quick Spin Oligo column (as used for RNA probes) to retain the oligonucleotide.

substeps.instruction: Invert the mini Quick Spin column, then return it to the correct orientation to settle the sepharose at the bottom; remove the top and bottom caps according to the product instructions.
Place the column into a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube and spin at 1000 × g for 30 s at room temperature; discard the tube.
Transfer the column to a new 1.5 mL screw‑cap tube.

steps.title: Dilute probe on column
steps.instruction: Add water to the column to bring the probe volume to 50 µL and carefully pipette the solution onto the centre of the sepharose matrix inside the column.

steps.title: Collect probe by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the column at 1000 × g for 4 min (temperature not specified) to elute the probe.

steps.title: Test radioactive incorporation
steps.instruction: Hold the probe and the column at equal distances from a Geiger counter using tweezers; at least 50 % of the label should be incorporated (the counts from the column and the probe should be equal). Discard the column in radioactive waste.

steps.title: Add probe to hybridization bottle
steps.instruction: While holding the bottle vertically, add the probe so it falls directly into the hybridization buffer and incubate overnight at 42 °C.

steps.title: Store probe for future use
steps.instruction: Transfer the probe to a 50 mL Falcon/Corning tube and store at –20 °C. RNA or DNA probes can be reused up to two additional times (three total uses) within one to two weeks, considering the isotope half‑life. To reuse: pre‑hybridize the membrane with half the normal volume of hybridization buffer, defrost the probe by placing the tube in a beaker of hot water for 20 min, then add the probe to the hybridization bottle.

steps.title: Low‑stringency wash
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane with 6× SSC for 10 min at 42 °C.

steps.title: High‑stringency wash
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane with pre‑heated 2× SSC containing 0.1 % SDS for 10 min at 42 °C.

steps.title: Final room‑temperature wash
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane with 50 mL of 6× SSC for 10 min at room temperature. (Optional: two 30‑min washes with 2× SSC 0.5 % SDS at 42 °C can improve signal‑to‑noise but may reduce signal for some probes.)
